It also never calls scrubTabFromPanes, so host.panes retains stale tabId strings after the wipe. persistTabs() then persists those stale pane references to localStorage, unlike closeTab and closeOtherTabs which always call scrubTabFromPanes or dropTab per-ID.
findings.suggested_fix: Before blanking host.tabs, iterate host.openTabs and call host.dropTab(id) + host.pruneTabUi(id) for each. Then call scrubTabFromPanes or reset host.panes to [{ tabId: null }] (single empty pane) before persistTabs(), matching the teardown contract established in closeTab and closeOtherTabs.

findings.title: restoreTabs double-loads on startup — active-tab load silently overwritten by focused-pane load
findings.description: restoreTabs first loads the persisted active tab (lines 244-248, setting currentConvoId), then unconditionally loads the focused-pane tab a second time if it differs (lines 265-267). The second loadConversation overwrites currentConvoId, making the first load wasted I/O. If the focused pane's tab is NOT in conversations meta (an edge-case after data loss), the condition at line 265 is true but loadConversation may fail, leaving currentConvoId set to the wrong value from the first call. The intent is for the focused pane to win, but the double-load is an unnecessary race.
findings.suggested_fix: Determine which tab should be active (focused pane tab if present, else active, else first valid) in one pass before any loadConversation call, then issue a single await host.loadConversation(winner). This removes the redundant I/O and the implicit overwrite.

findings.title: restoreTabs silently swallows errors, leaving state partially mutated
findings.description: The catch block in restoreTabs() only emits a console.warn and returns. If JSON.parse or a loadConversation() call throws after host.openTabs has already been written (line 242) but before pane restoration completes, the store is left in a half-restored state — openTabs contains ids but panes/focusedPaneIdx are still at their defaults — with no indication to the caller or UI that restoration failed. The finally ensures persistTabs() runs, which then persists the corrupted intermediate state back to localStorage.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset state on failure before persistTabs() runs: in the catch block, reset host.openTabs to [] and host.panes to [{ tabId: null }] so persistTabs() writes a clean empty state rather than a partial one. Optionally surface the error via host.lastNotice or host.telemetry.event('tabs.restore.error', ...) so the UI can show a notice.

findings.title: Greeting computed once at mount, not reactive — stale across hour boundaries
findings.description: `greeting()` is called once as a plain `const` at component instantiation, not wrapped in `$derived`. The result is frozen for the lifetime of the component. If the welcome screen stays mounted across a time-of-day boundary (e.g. the user leaves Rift open overnight), it will show the wrong greeting indefinitely. In a Svelte 5 runes file every reactive value should be `$derived`; a bare `const` initialized from a runtime call is the Svelte-4 `let` / `$:` antipattern in disguise.
findings.evidence: const greet = greeting();
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `const greet = $derived(greeting());` so the value is re-evaluated whenever the component's reactive graph is invalidated. For true clock-driven freshness, drive it from a `$state` tick or the existing date utilities, but `$derived` at minimum prevents stale display after long idle.

findings.title: $effect calls loadWorkspaceBranch unconditionally on every workspace change — no load guard
findings.description: The second `$effect` fires `loadWorkspaceBranch()` every time `assistant.workspace.current` is truthy and any reactive dependency re-runs — there is no guard checking whether the branch is already loaded or an in-flight fetch is pending. If any unrelated reactive state touched by the effect's body changes (e.g. a parent re-renders this component), `loadWorkspaceBranch` is called again, potentially issuing duplicate IPC/async calls. The companion effect on line 79-83 correctly guards with `workspaceFiles.length === 0`; the branch effect lacks an equivalent guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a guard mirroring the files effect: `if (assistant.workspace.current && assistant.workspaceBranch == null) void assistant.loadWorkspaceBranch();` — or make `loadWorkspaceBranch` internally idempotent (no-op if result already cached) and document that assumption here.

findings.title: Icon-only 'Forget' button has no accessible label
findings.description: The 'Forget' (×) button renders only an X icon with a tooltip action. Tooltips are mouse-only; screen readers announce nothing meaningful for this button, making it opaque to keyboard/AT users.
findings.evidence:
<button
                  class="wel-recent-x"
                  type="button"
                  use:tooltip={"Forget"}
                  onclick={() => void assistant.removeRecentRoot(r)}
                ><X size={11}/></button>
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label="Forget {leafName(r)}" directly on the button element so the accessible name matches the tooltip text and is scoped to the specific folder.

findings.title: O(N²) flat.indexOf(it) called per rendered item inside #each
findings.description: `{@const idx = flat.indexOf(it)}` is evaluated for every item in every `g.items` inner loop. `flat` is an array derived from `grouped`, so each call scans up to N elements, making the render O(N²). With ~15 items today this is benign, but the pattern will degrade visibly if `assistant.conversations` grows (e.g. hundreds of chats). The index is already deterministic from the outer group structure and can be pre-computed in O(N).
findings.evidence:
{#each g.items as it (it.id)}
  {@const idx = flat.indexOf(it)}
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-build an index map once in a `$derived`: `const flatIdx = $derived(new Map(flat.map((it, i) => [it.id, i])))`, then replace `flat.indexOf(it)` with `flatIdx.get(it.id) ?? 0`. This reduces the render loop to O(N).

findings.title: aria-pressed misused on navigation buttons — wrong AT semantic
findings.description: Both the top-group workspace buttons (line 164) and the Settings button (line 202) use aria-pressed, which declares them as toggle buttons to screen readers. These are navigation items that switch the active view, not stateful toggles. Screen readers announce them as 'pressed/not pressed' toggle controls rather than navigation items. The correct pattern is role="tab" with aria-selected, or a <nav> with role="tab" descendants (the wrapping <nav> exists but the buttons lack the tab role).
findings.evidence: aria-pressed={isActive}
findings.suggested_fix: Replace aria-pressed={isActive} with role="tab" aria-selected={isActive} on the buttons, and add role="tablist" to the parent .ab-group div. Alternatively, if tab semantics don't fit the design, use aria-current="page" (or aria-current="true") which is the standard for navigation current-item without implying a toggle.

findings.title: pointermove/pointerup handlers on individual buttons instead of container — drag breaks silently when pointer capture fails
findings.description: onpointermove and onpointerup are registered on each individual <button> (lines 166-167) rather than on the container. The code relies on setPointerCapture to route all pointer events to the capturing element, but the capture call is inside a swallowed try/catch (line 47-49). If capture fails (element detaches, unsupported context), pointermove and pointerup only fire while the pointer is physically over a button — gaps between buttons and fast drags past the group boundary silently stop updating dragDeltaY and dropSlot, leaving the drag in an inconsistent visual state with no error surfaced.
findings.evidence:
onpointermove={onPointerMove}
        onpointerup={onPointerUp}
findings.suggested_fix: Attach onpointermove, onpointerup, and onpointercancel to the container div.ab-top (which already has bind:this={topRowEl}) rather than each button. This makes drag tracking container-scoped and capture-failure-resilient. The swallowed catch on setPointerCapture should at minimum set a flag so the fallback path is known to be active.

findings.title: $effect reads then writes fracs causing a redundant re-run
findings.description: The $effect at line 94 both READS `fracs.length` (tracking `fracs` as a dependency) and WRITES `fracs` on the same code path. On every pane-count change the effect fires, writes a new array to `fracs`, which marks `fracs` dirty, causing the effect to re-run a second time. The second run finds `fracs.length === n` and exits, so it terminates, but the double-run is wasteful and the pattern is fragile — any future change that keeps `fracs.length` equal but changes content would loop. The correct Svelte 5 pattern is to derive the new array from `assistant.panes.length` without reading `fracs` insi
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `fracs` from the effect's tracked reads by caching the old length in a separate non-reactive variable, or restructure so the effect only reads `assistant.panes.length` (an unambiguous external source) and computes the new array without consulting `fracs.length`: e.g. `const n = assistant.panes.length || 1; fracs = loadFracs(n);` guarded by `untrack(() => fracs.length) !== n` to avoid the dependency on `fracs`.

findings.title: greeting() computed outside reactive context — stale across hour boundaries
findings.description: greeting() is called once at component instantiation and stored in a plain const. If the component stays mounted past a hour boundary (e.g. 11:59 → 12:00), the eyebrow text never updates. Should be $derived(greeting()) so Svelte can re-evaluate when the component re-renders.
findings.evidence: const greet = greeting();
findings.suggested_fix: const greet = $derived(greeting()); — or, if real-time updates are wanted, drive it from a $state(new Date()) that a setInterval updates.

findings.title: $effect async branch load — no in-flight cancellation (stale-write race)
findings.description: The $effect fires `loadWorkspaceBranch()` every time `assistant.workspace.current` changes. There is no AbortController or in-flight guard: if the user rapidly switches folders (or if the reactive graph re-triggers), multiple concurrent `invoke('assistant_workspace_branch')` calls race to write `host.workspaceBranch`. Whichever call resolves last wins, which may be an older result for a superseded root — silently setting the wrong branch label on the current workspace.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the current root at call-start and discard the result if it changed before resolution, or add a simple monotonic call-id guard in `loadWorkspaceBranch`: capture the root before `await invoke(...)`, and after it resolves check `host.workspace.current === captured` before writing. Alternatively wrap in a debounce (e.g. 150 ms) so rapid changes collapse to one call.

findings.title: Branch-load error silently swallowed — not surfaced to UI (fail-loud violation)
findings.description: When `invoke('assistant_workspace_branch')` throws (Tauri command error, workspace not a git repo, etc.) the catch block in `loadWorkspaceBranch` emits only `console.warn` and sets `workspaceBranch = null`. The dashboard hero silently shows no branch — the user sees no indication that the branch read failed. Per project rules (fail-loud), errors from `invoke()` must be surfaced rather than swallowed.
findings.suggested_fix: Either propagate the error to a visible diagnostic (toast / inline badge on the Workspace card) or, at minimum, set a boolean `workspaceBranchError` flag on state so the UI can render a 'branch unavailable' hint instead of silently showing nothing.

findings.title: Empty catch silently swallows non-compat errors in onFocus
findings.description: The catch block at line 200-202 swallows ALL exceptions thrown by node.matches(':focus-visible'), not just the expected NotSupportedError from old engines. Any unrelated DOM error (e.g. detached node) is silently discarded, violating the project rule 'Async errors must be caught or propagated — never swallow with empty catch'. Should narrow the catch to only the expected compatibility error.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the catch: `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof DOMException)) throw e; }` — or check `CSS.supports('selector(:focus-visible)')` once at module init and skip the try/catch entirely.

findings.title: lastNotice not cleared on compaction failure paths
findings.description: host.lastNotice is set to 'Compacting conversation…' at line 117, then updated only on the success path (line 230). Both early-return failure branches (line 174: summarize returned null; line 185: remint failed) set host.lastError but never clear lastNotice. The finally block only resets compactingNow. After any failed compact the UI simultaneously shows the stale 'Compacting…' notice and the error string.
findings.suggested_fix: In the finally block (or immediately before each failure return), set host.lastNotice = null when host.lastError is being set, so the stale in-progress notice is cleared on every non-success exit.

findings.title: Unsafe non-null cast on import.meta.hot bypasses type safety
findings.description: Line 235 casts import.meta to { hot: { dispose: ... } } (non-optional hot) and immediately calls .hot.dispose(). Although guarded by the runtime if-check on line 234 (which uses the optional variant hot?:), the cast on line 235 strips the undefined type, hiding the fact that this code path only runs when hot is truthy. If the if-condition ever changes or is accidentally removed, the non-optional cast makes tsc think .hot is always present and will not warn.
findings.evidence: (import.meta as { hot: { dispose: (cb: () => void) => void } }).hot.dispose(() => updates.dispose());

findings.title: invoke('app_version') error swallowed — fail-loud violation
findings.description: The catch block for `app_version` only emits a `console.warn` and lets execution continue with `currentVersion` stuck at `'?'`. No user-visible signal is set, and `this.state` is never set to `'error'` for this path. The fail-loud rule requires visible failure over silent fallback — a warn log is not visible to the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `this.error` (or a separate `versionError`) and either surface a toast or set `this.state = 'error'` so the UI reflects the failed probe. At minimum, propagate the error string so the dialog doesn't silently show 'v? → v1.2.3'.

findings.title: Root-cause download error lost in fallback catch — downloadError shows wrong error
findings.description: `downloadError` is set to `String(e2 ?? e)`. Because `e2` comes from the `openUrl` fallback (a secondary failure), it shadows the original `e` from `download_update`/`openPath` whenever `e2` is truthy. The user and any telemetry see only the fallback-open error, not the root cause (e.g. disk full, permission denied on the downloaded file). The `?? e` fallback only fires when `e2` is nullish, which is not the typical throw path.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve both errors: e.g. `this.downloadError = String(e2) + (e !== e2 ? ` (after: ${String(e)})` : '')`, or log `e` separately and surface only `e2` to the user while keeping `e` in console/telemetry.

findings.title: openMenu with empty options array sets highlight=0, keyboard pick dereferences undefined
findings.description: When `options` is empty, `options.findIndex(...)` returns -1, `Math.max(0, -1)` sets `highlight = 0`. Then pressing Enter/Space on the open (empty) menu hits `if (options[highlight]) pick(options[highlight])` at line 84 — `options[0]` is `undefined`, so the guard saves it. However `moveHighlight` at line 97 calls `(0 + dir + 0) % 0` which is `NaN` (division by zero via modulo), then `options[NaN]` is `undefined` and `options[NaN]?.disabled` is `undefined` (falsy), so the loop exits with `highlight = NaN`. Subsequent renders with `i === highlight` checks become unreliable.
findings.evidence: highlight = Math.max(0, options.findIndex((o) => o.value === value));
findings.suggested_fix: Guard openMenu: `if (!options.length) return;` before setting highlight, or clamp: `highlight = options.length ? Math.max(0, options.findIndex(...)) : -1;`.

findings.title: disabled button hides options from AT instead of announcing them as unavailable
findings.description: Options use `<button role="option" disabled={o.disabled}>`. The native `disabled` attribute removes the element from the accessibility tree entirely, so screen-reader users never hear that a disabled option exists. ARIA spec for `listbox` expects `aria-disabled="true"` on the `option` (keeping it announced) rather than the HTML `disabled` attribute which suppresses it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `disabled={o.disabled}` with `aria-disabled={o.disabled}` and guard the click handler: `onclick={() => { if (o.disabled) return; pick(o); }}`. This keeps disabled options visible to AT while still preventing interaction.

findings.title: data: URI passthrough to native webview without sanitization
findings.description: normalizeUrl explicitly allows data: URIs to pass through unsanitized. These URLs are forwarded verbatim to invoke("browser_open") and invoke("browser_navigate") in the native child webview. A data: URI (e.g. data:text/html,<script>alert(1)<\/script>) can execute arbitrary HTML/JS in the child webview context. If any other feature (assistant tool output, history, or future auto-fill) can populate the address field programmatically, this is a direct XSS vector into the embedded browser.
findings.evidence: if (/^[a-z]+:\/\//i.test(t) || t.startsWith("data:")) return t;
findings.suggested_fix: Block data: URIs at the normalizeUrl level (or before invoke). Only allow http: and https: schemes: `if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(t)) return t;` — reject everything else (data:, javascript:, file:, blob:) with an error message set on the `error` state.

findings.title: Async checkOnLaunch() return value silently discarded in $effect
findings.description: updates.checkOnLaunch() is async but its Promise is not awaited or void-annotated inside the $effect. Any rejection (e.g. Tauri invoke failure inside refresh()) becomes an unhandled Promise rejection with no visible error. The rest of the codebase consistently uses `void fn()` when intentionally discarding async results (lines 53, 63, 69, 74).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `void` to signal intentional discard: `void updates.checkOnLaunch();` — or wrap in a try/catch inside an async IIFE if you want to surface errors to the UI.

findings.title: Async keyboard-handler rejections silently swallowed
findings.description: All async assistant calls inside onGlobalKey are void-cast (lines 53, 63, 69, 74), discarding their Promise rejections entirely. A failure in assistant.openTab / newTab / closeTab / cycleTab produces no user-visible feedback and no console error — silent failure on a keyboard action. This violates the project's fail-loud rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each call: assistant.newTab().catch(e => toast.error(String(e))) (or equivalent toast/notification pattern used elsewhere in the project) so failures surface to the user.

findings.title: Cold-start metrics silently null when turn[0] fails the modelId filter
findings.description: The `i === 0` cold-start block (lines 126-130) sits after the `continue` guard at line 67. If the very first turn has `modelId == null` and `endKind !== 'success'` (e.g. an aborted or error turn), the loop skips it entirely, so `firstTurnCostUsd` and `coldStartCacheCreate` remain `null` for the whole session — even though turn[0] may have real cost/cacheCreate data. The guard was designed to filter phantom model-bucket entries, but as a side effect it gates the cold-start recording that should be unconditional.
findings.evidence: if (t.modelId == null && t.endKind !== "success") continue;
findings.suggested_fix: Move the cold-start block (lines 126-130) to before the `continue` guard, or hoist it into a separate pre-loop pass over `this.turns[0]` so it always runs regardless of the filter.

findings.title: Inner `const u` shadows outer `const u` in the same loop iteration
findings.description: Line 77 declares `const u = t.resultUsage || t.envelopeUsage` in the loop body. Line 142 re-declares `const u = t.resultUsage || t.envelopeUsage` inside a nested `if` block within the same iteration. The two `u` bindings are identical expressions, so there is no runtime difference now, but shadowing the outer name means a future reader (or refactor) can silently change one without affecting the other. TypeScript allows block-scoped shadowing and emits no warning by default; tsconfig `noShadow` is not universally enabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the inner `const u` declaration and reuse the outer `u` already in scope at line 77 — the expression is identical, so no logic change is needed.

findings.title: O(n²) per-model timing average recalculates over all turns for each model key
findings.description: After the main loop, `summarize()` iterates `Object.keys(byModel)` and for each model key re-filters `this.turns` with `.filter()` then re-maps twice. With M distinct models and N total turns this is O(M×N). For typical session sizes this is negligible, but the data to compute per-model averages is already available inside the main loop (ttfp and done timestamps per-model could be accumulated into per-bucket arrays there). The current approach also re-evaluates `(t.modelId || t.model) === key` for every turn for every model, duplicating the bucket-key logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `ttfps: number[]` and `doneTimes: number[]` arrays to each bucket initializer at line 69-74. In the main loop, push values there directly (mirroring the global `ttfps`/`doneTimes` arrays). Then the per-model average block at lines 150-157 becomes a simple reduce over the pre-accumulated arrays — one O(N) pass total instead of O(M×N).

findings.title: snapshot() calls Date.now() twice, producing inconsistent capturedAt vs durationMs
findings.description: `capturedAt` and `durationMs` are computed from two separate `Date.now()` calls on lines 19 and 20. In normal execution the skew is sub-millisecond, but under a slow GC pause or scheduler delay the two values can diverge: `durationMs` would then not equal `capturedAt - startedAt`. A consumer diffing `snapshot.capturedAt - snapshot.startedAt` against `snapshot.durationMs` would see a discrepancy, which could confuse diagnostics tooling.
findings.evidence:
capturedAt: Date.now(),
      durationMs: Date.now() - this.startedAt,
findings.suggested_fix: Capture once: `const now = Date.now();` before the return, then use `capturedAt: now` and `durationMs: now - this.startedAt`.

findings.title: onComplete fires after component may be destroyed
findings.description: The `finally` block sets `exiting = true` then `await sleep(exitMs)` before calling `onComplete()`. If the parent unmounts SplashOverlay during that sleep (e.g. fast HMR reload, double-mount), the async continuation resumes on a destroyed component: `exiting` write is a no-op on dead state and `onComplete` is called against a stale closure. No crash, but the parent's completion handler fires unexpectedly after teardown.
findings.suggested_fix: Track a destroyed flag via `onDestroy` and guard the continuation: `let destroyed = false; onDestroy(() => { destroyed = true; }); ... if (!destroyed) onComplete();`

findings.title: aria-hidden bound to string literal 'false' rather than boolean false
findings.description: `aria-hidden={exiting ? 'true' : 'false'}` always renders as a string attribute. When not exiting the DOM gets `aria-hidden="false"` — the string `"false"` is technically valid WAI-ARIA but some assistive technologies treat any non-absent value of `aria-hidden` as truthy. The idiomatic Svelte 5 / HTML pattern is to omit the attribute entirely when false, or bind a boolean: `aria-hidden={exiting || undefined}`.
findings.evidence: aria-hidden={exiting ? "true" : "false"}
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with `aria-hidden={exiting || undefined}` — Svelte omits the attribute when the value is `undefined`, which is the correct semantic for "not hidden".

findings.title: aria-live region never emits text — screen readers get no completion announcement
findings.description: The root div carries `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` but its inner content is purely visual (a wordmark text node and an animated bar). No text update is injected into the live region when loading completes, so screen readers that depend on live-region announcements receive no feedback that the splash finished. Additionally, `aria-hidden="false"` is a no-op (the attribute should simply be absent when not hidden).
findings.evidence:
role="status"
  aria-live="polite"
  aria-label="Loading Rift"
  aria-hidden={exiting ? "true" : "false"}
findings.suggested_fix: Add a visually-hidden `<span class="sr-only">` inside the live region and update its text to 'Ready' when `exiting` becomes true. Replace `aria-hidden={exiting ? 'true' : 'false'}` with `{#if exiting}aria-hidden="true"{/if}` (or omit the attribute entirely when false).

findings.title: Unsafe `any` icon prop flows into component invocation
findings.description: item.icon is typed `any` (deliberately, per comment in toast.svelte.ts). At line 23, `Icon` is inferred as `any`, so `<Icon size={12}/>` at line 45 is an untyped component call — TypeScript cannot verify the prop contract. A caller passing a non-component value (e.g. a string) would compile silently and crash at runtime.
findings.evidence: {@const Icon = item.icon ?? SEVERITY_ICON[item.severity]}
findings.suggested_fix: Type icon as `typeof Info | undefined` (or a union of the known Lucide icon constructors / `ComponentType`) in ToastItem. The comment says it fights lucide-svelte type defs, but `import type { Icon as LucideIcon } from 'lucide-svelte'` provides a proper constructor type that resolves the conflict.

findings.title: Svelte fly transitions ignore prefers-reduced-motion
findings.description: The @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block at line 175 only strips CSS `transition` from .toast, but the Svelte `in:fly` and `out:fly` directives (lines 41-42) are JS-driven animations that bypass CSS media queries entirely. Users who have enabled the OS reduced-motion preference will still see fly-in/fly-out animations on every toast.
findings.evidence:
in:fly={{ y: 10, duration: 200 }}
      out:fly={{ y: 6, duration: 140 }}
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the transition parameters on the media query. In the script block: `const reducedMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;` then use `in:fly={{ y: reducedMotion ? 0 : 10, duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 200 }}` (and same for out:fly). Alternatively use a Svelte crossfade/fade transition instead of fly when reduced motion is active.

findings.title: Unvalidated localStorage spread into typed CodePrefs state
findings.description: The parsed object from localStorage is spread directly into `this.code` with only an `object` type check — no validation that `fontSize`/`tabWidth` are numbers or `ligatures` is a boolean. A stored string like `"12"` for fontSize passes through and is later written verbatim into the `--code-fs` CSS custom property as `"12px"` (line 157), which works accidentally; but `tabWidth` or `ligatures` with wrong runtime types silently corrupt CSS vars. The `catch` only catches `JSON.parse` failures, not type mismatches.
findings.evidence:
const c = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(CODE_KEY) ?? "null");
      if (c && typeof c === "object") this.code = { ...DEFAULT_CODE, ...c };
findings.suggested_fix: Validate each property before spreading: `const fontSize = typeof c.fontSize === 'number' ? c.fontSize : DEFAULT_CODE.fontSize;` (etc.) or use a zod/valibot schema. At minimum check `typeof c.tabWidth === 'number' && typeof c.ligatures === 'boolean'` before accepting the parsed value.

findings.title: Redundant as-cast suppresses TypeScript narrowing on navItems
findings.description: workspace.order is already typed $state<WorkspaceId[]>, so .filter() already returns WorkspaceId[]. The trailing `as WorkspaceId[]` cast is a no-op today but will silently widen the type if WorkspaceId ever gains new variants or the filter predicate changes, hiding the mismatch from TypeScript instead of surfacing a compile error.
findings.evidence: workspace.order.filter((id) => id !== "settings") as WorkspaceId[]
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the cast; if a narrower type is needed (e.g. Exclude<WorkspaceId, 'settings'>[]) express it explicitly rather than casting.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejections on window control buttons
findings.description: win.minimize(), win.toggleMaximize(), and win.close() return Promises that are silently dropped. If the Tauri IPC call fails (e.g. permission error or WebView race), the error is swallowed with no user feedback — violates fail-loud.
findings.evidence: onclick={() => win.minimize()} use:tooltip={"Minimize"}
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each call: onclick={() => win.minimize().catch(console.error)} or create a shared handler that logs/toasts on rejection. At minimum add .catch(console.error) so failures surface in DevTools.

findings.title: setTimeout handle in copyCommand not cancelled on teardown — stale closure leak
findings.description: `copyCommand` starts a 1600ms `setTimeout` to reset `this.copied` but never stores the handle, so it cannot be cancelled. If the owning component unmounts before the timer fires, the callback still executes and mutates `this.copied` on a stale class instance. In Svelte 5 runes this is harmless if nothing holds a DOM reference, but repeated rapid calls stack unbounded timers and the pattern is a leak footgun if the class gains any cleanup logic later.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the handle and cancel on re-entry: `if (this._copyTimer) clearTimeout(this._copyTimer); this._copyTimer = setTimeout(() => { this.copied = false; this._copyTimer = null; }, 1600);`. Add `private _copyTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;` as a class field.

findings.title: $state<Set> initial seed 'chat' is stale if stored activeId differs — brief pre-init flash
findings.description: The `everOpened` field is initialised with `new Set(["chat"])` at class construction time (line 65). If `init()` is called asynchronously (e.g., inside `onMount`), any reactive subscriber that reads `workspace.everOpened` during the first render tick will see 'chat' as already-opened even when the stored active workspace is 'settings' or 'home'. This causes the lazy-mount guard to skip unmounting 'chat' for that tick, keeping its component mounted unnecessarily until the next reactive flush after `init()` reassigns `everOpened` on line 78.
findings.evidence: everOpened = $state<Set<WorkspaceId>>(new Set(["chat"]));
findings.suggested_fix: Initialise `everOpened` to an empty Set (`new Set<WorkspaceId>()`) and let `init()` seed it authoritatively. Alternatively, ensure `init()` is called synchronously before first render (module-level or in the layout's `load` function rather than `onMount`).

findings.title: Silent swallow of JSON.parse failure in init()
findings.description: The catch block at line 93 silently discards any JSON.parse or filter error from the persisted ORDER_KEY value with only a comment. If localStorage contains corrupted/unexpected data the failure is invisible — the user sees no feedback and `order` silently falls back to default, making persistence bugs hard to diagnose. Project rules mandate fail-loud (visible failure > silent fallback; never swallow errors).
findings.evidence: } catch { /* parse fail → default order */ }
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum log the error: `catch (e) { console.warn('[workspace] ORDER_KEY parse failed, using default:', e); }`. If Rift has a diagnostics bus (DiagBus in diagnostics/mod.rs), forward it there so it surfaces in the UI log. Do not silently drop it.

findings.title: everOpened Set allocation on every first-visit setActive() call allocates unnecessarily but is low-risk
findings.description: Each time a workspace is visited for the first time, `setActive` creates a brand-new Set via spread (`new Set([...this.everOpened, id])`). With only 3 WorkspaceIds this is negligible, but the pattern triggers full Svelte 5 reactivity propagation on every such call because a new object reference is assigned to `$state`. A `.add()` mutation with an explicit reassignment trigger would be cleaner and consistent with the project's immutable-update pattern.
findings.evidence: this.everOpened = new Set([...this.everOpened, id]);
findings.suggested_fix: Consider: `this.everOpened = new Set(this.everOpened); this.everOpened.add(id);` — still a new Set (needed for Svelte 5 reactivity) but avoids the spread-of-spread. Alternatively keep current pattern given the tiny Set size; the issue is cosmetic at this scale.

findings.title: Unsafe `as Persisted` cast — activeIdx and tab fields unvalidated
findings.description: `JSON.parse(raw) as Persisted` only validates `tabs` is an array; it never checks that `activeIdx` is a number or that each tab object has the required string fields. A corrupted/tampered localStorage entry where `activeIdx` is null, a string, or absent passes `Math.min(null, ...)` via JS coercion (yields 0 — survivable but wrong type contract). Tab entries with missing fields (e.g., no `id`) silently produce `undefined` in later lookups. The `as` cast is a lie to the type system.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the cast with a type-guard: check `typeof parsed.activeIdx === 'number'` and validate each tab entry has the four required string fields before returning. Alternatively, use a zod/valibot schema for one-line parse+validate.

findings.title: Dead SFTP `remotePath` field baked into type and all mutation paths
findings.description: `BrowserTab.remotePath` and the `defaultRemote` parameter on `hydrate()` are SFTP-era remnants. The SFTP/sync/server half was fully stripped on 2026-06-03 (per CLAUDE.md). Every `open()` and `updateRemotePath()` call, and every persisted tab object, carries a `remotePath` string that is never read by any consumer. It bloats localStorage and forces every call-site to pass a meaningless argument. `updateRemotePath` (lines 125-131) is entirely dead.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `remotePath` from `BrowserTab`, drop `defaultRemote` from `hydrate()`, delete `updateRemotePath()`, and update all call-sites. Run `svelte-check` + `cargo check` after to catch any Rust IPC consumers.

findings.title: Unsanitized localStorage deserialization — no field-level validation on BrowserTab
findings.description: loadPersisted() casts the JSON.parse result directly to Persisted after only checking Array.isArray(parsed.tabs). Individual BrowserTab fields (id, name, localPath, remotePath) are never validated for type or content. Corrupt or attacker-controlled localStorage data (e.g. localPath: null, or a path-traversal string) passes into $state and can reach MCP backend tools (read_file/list_dir/grep) without any sanitization at the boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: After the array check, validate each element: confirm typeof tab.id/name/localPath/remotePath === 'string', and optionally reject entries where localPath contains traversal sequences ('..') before returning. Reject the whole persisted block if any tab fails.

findings.title: Silent empty catch on localStorage.removeItem in reset()
findings.description: reset() wraps localStorage.removeItem in try/catch {} with an empty catch body. Any storage error (QuotaExceededError, SecurityError in a sandboxed context) is swallowed with no log or state signal, violating the project's fail-loud rule. The companion savePersisted() correctly emits console.warn — reset() should do the same.
findings.evidence: try { localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY); } catch {}
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the empty catch with: catch (e) { console.warn('browser-tabs reset failed', e); }

findings.title: Page title rendered as <span>, not a heading element
findings.description: The `title` prop is output in a `<span>` inside a `<header>` landmark. Screen readers won't announce it as a page or section heading; users navigating by heading (H key in NVDA/JAWS) will skip it entirely. A `<h1>`/`<h2>` (or `role="heading" aria-level="2"`) is the correct element for a page-level title inside a landmark region.
findings.evidence: {title}
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace `` with `

` (and close with `

`). Adjust font/weight in CSS if the visual size changes (it shouldn't — styles are class-bound). If only one PageHeader is ever mounted per page, `h1` is appropriate instead.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection on Shiki init failure
findings.description: whenReady() is called with no .catch(). If createHighlighterCore rejects (e.g. network error fetching a language grammar bundle in a constrained env), the promise rejection is unhandled. In browser environments this fires window.onunhandledrejection and can surface as a console error or crash reporter event. shikiReady stays false forever, silently degrading all code blocks to plain text with no user feedback.
findings.evidence: whenReady().then(() => { shikiReady = true; });
findings.suggested_fix: Add a .catch: whenReady().then(() => { shikiReady = true; }).catch(() => { /* shiki unavailable; plain-text fallback stays active */ });

findings.title: toast.resume() resets to full timeout, ignoring elapsed time
findings.description: pause() calls clearTimer which deletes the timer entry. resume() then reschedules using item.timeoutMs ?? defaultTimeout(item.severity) — the original full duration. Any time the toast was already visible before the hover is completely discarded; hovering a toast that had 500ms left restarts it with 4000ms. The check `if (this.timers.has(id)) return` on line 84 is also wrong: after pause the map has no entry, so the guard never fires and resume always creates a new full-duration timer.
findings.suggested_fix: Track a `startedAt` timestamp and `remainingMs` per toast. On pause, compute remaining = ms - (Date.now() - startedAt). On resume, schedule with remaining instead of the full duration. Alternatively, store the deadline timestamp and use Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()) in resume.

findings.title: Re-exported WorkspaceId leaks an unrelated module's public surface
findings.description: Line 37 re-exports `WorkspaceId` from `workspace.svelte` through the command-palette module. Nothing in this file uses it — it's a stray export that couples two unrelated modules, bloats the public API of command-palette, and will cause a broken import if `workspace.svelte` ever renames or drops that type. Any consumer currently importing `WorkspaceId` from this path will silently break on a rename, with no compile-time link back to the real source.
findings.evidence: export type { WorkspaceId };
findings.suggested_fix: Remove line 37. Consumers that need `WorkspaceId` should import it directly from `./workspace.svelte`.

findings.title: accessibility.init() silently discards persisted state when localStorage throws (no try/catch)
findings.description: `init()` calls `localStorage.getItem` and `localStorage.setItem` (indirectly via `setDyslexiaMode`) without any try/catch. In private-browsing / storage-quota-exceeded / cross-origin iframe scenarios, these throw `DOMException`. `browserDock` wraps its localStorage writes in try/catch (line 27-28 of that file), but `accessibility` does not guard its reads in `init()` or its writes in `setFont`, `setLineHeightBoost`, `setWarmTint`. An exception in `init()` leaves the class in a partially-initialised state (e.g. `dyslexiaMode` set but `font`/`lineHeightBoost` not yet restored), and the exception
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the body of `init()` (and the `localStorage.setItem` calls in the setter methods) in try/catch, matching the pattern already used in `browserDock.toggle()` and `setWidth()`.

findings.title: loadWorkspaceFiles de-dup guard never prevents stale overwrites on root change
findings.description: The concurrent-call guard compares `workspaceFilesLoadingFor === root`, but the guard is only checked at call entry, not re-validated after the async invoke resolves. If the user switches workspace root while the invoke is in-flight, the finally block resets `workspaceFilesLoadingFor = null` and `workspaceFiles` is overwritten with the result for the *old* root — now displayed under the new root. No cancellation token, no post-await root check.
findings.suggested_fix: After the await, re-check that `host.workspace.current === root` before assigning: `if (host.workspace.current === root) host.workspaceFiles = result;` — and only then clear the guard.

findings.title: Swallowed action errors: run() always closes menu and discards failures silently
findings.description: run() catches any rejection from fn() with console.warn and then unconditionally calls onClose(). If a Tauri invoke fails (e.g. open_in_vscode backend error), the clipboard is unavailable, or openPath rejects, the user sees no feedback — the menu simply disappears as though the action succeeded. Violates the project rule 'async errors must be caught or propagated — never swallow with empty catch'.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface failures to the user: either toast the error message before closing (e.g. a brief error state in the menu) or re-throw after logging so callers can handle it. At minimum, move onClose() inside the try block so it only fires on success.

findings.title: Global event listeners leak if component unmounts before setTimeout fires
findings.description: The mousedown and keydown listeners are registered inside a setTimeout(..., 0). If the component is destroyed (onMount cleanup runs) before that zero-delay timeout fires, the cleanup removes listeners that haven't been added yet — they then get added after cleanup, permanently, on document. Every subsequent mousedown/keydown calls the stale onClose closure with no way to remove it.
findings.suggested_fix: Track whether the component is still mounted and skip the addEventListener calls if already destroyed: add `let destroyed = false;` before the setTimeout, set `destroyed = true` in the cleanup, and guard the addEventListener calls with `if (!destroyed)`.

findings.title: tone prop silently no-ops when icon is omitted
findings.description: The data-tone attribute is applied exclusively inside the {#if icon} block on .empty-glyph. When icon is not passed, the tone prop is accepted and type-checked but has zero effect — no element receives the tone styling. Callers passing tone="danger" or tone="warn" without an icon silently get the default accent appearance with no error or visual feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Either apply a tone class to the root .empty div unconditionally (e.g. data-tone={tone} on the outer <div class="empty">) so tone affects title/hint color when no icon is present, or document that tone requires icon and add a runtime assertion in dev mode.

findings.title: aria-hidden suppresses the only accessible name on the logo image
findings.description: The carries both alt="Rift" and aria-hidden="true". aria-hidden removes the element from the accessibility tree entirely, making the alt text unreachable to screen readers. If the logo is purely decorative this should be alt="" (empty string); if it conveys brand identity the aria-hidden should be removed. The current combination is contradictory and leaves assistive technology users with neither a label nor a decorative skip.
findings.suggested_fix: Decorative use: change alt="" and keep aria-hidden="true". Meaningful use (e.g. standalone logo on an onboarding screen): remove aria-hidden="true" and keep alt="Rift".

findings.title: dontAsk state not reset on external open→close→reopen cycle
findings.description: dontAsk=$state(false) is reset inside decide(), but if the parent closes the dialog by setting open=false without the user clicking a button (e.g. programmatic close or navigation), dontAsk is never reset. On the next open, the checkbox renders pre-checked (true) leaking state from the previous session.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a $effect that resets dontAsk whenever open transitions from true to false: `$effect(() => { if (!open) dontAsk = false; });`

findings.title: ~200+ lines of dead CSS for the stripped multi-step flow shipped in bundle
findings.description: The SFTP/sync/multi-step walkthrough was removed on 2026-06-03 but the CSS was not trimmed. Classes including `.ob-rail`, `.ob-steps`, `.ob-step`, `.ob-node`, `.ob-sync`, `.ob-sync-stage`, `.ob-bar`, `.ob-log`, `.ob-logline`, `.ob-summary`, `.ob-spill`, `.ob-choices`, `.ob-choice`, `.ob-confirm`, `.ob-ready`, `.ob-keybox`, `.ob-keycopy`, `.ob-accent`, `.ob-foot-dots`, `.ob-fdot`, `.ob-grid`, `.ob-divider`, `.ob-statcard`, `.ob-statrow`, `.ob-note` are unreferenced by any remaining Svelte component. Because the CSS is loaded globally (not scoped), it is not tree-shaken and ships into the prod b
findings.suggested_fix: Delete all CSS blocks whose selector classes are not referenced in any active .svelte file. A grep for each `.ob-*` class across `src/` will confirm which are orphaned. Leaving only the classes used by `OnboardingFlow.svelte`, `ObStage.svelte`, and `ClaudeAuth.svelte` will reduce the file by ~60%.

findings.title: Dead CSS alias referencing deleted SyncPage
findings.description: --muted alias is explicitly kept for SyncPage.svelte per the inline comment, but SyncPage was deleted in the 2026-06-03 pure-assistant conversion (confirmed in CLAUDE.md hot-files section). The rule is unreferenced dead weight — it won't cause a runtime bug but pollutes the token namespace and misleads future readers.
findings.evidence:
/* legacy alias kept for SyncPage.svelte — rest of shadcn aliases removed */
  --muted:               var(--bg-elev-2);
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the --muted declaration and its comment. Grep for any remaining `var(--muted)` references before deleting to confirm no other consumer exists.

findings.title: russh 0.60.2 — Unbounded 32-bit allocation (RUSTSEC-2026-0154)
findings.description: russh 0.60.2 allocates a buffer whose size is taken directly from a 32-bit field in the SSH packet without bounds checking, allowing a peer to trigger a multi-GB allocation and OOM-crash the process. Fix: upgrade to russh >=0.60.3. Reachability: russh is a direct dep (Cargo.toml line 51) and is compiled into the binary, but no live Rust source under src/ imports or calls it — the SSH/SFTP layer was stripped in the pure-assistant conversion (2026-06-03). The crate is linked dead weight; removing it from Cargo.toml eliminates the advisory entirely.
findings.evidence: russh = { version = "~0.60", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "rsa", "flate2", "async-trait"] }

findings.title: vitest: arbitrary file read & execute via Vitest UI server (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp)
findings.description: vitest <4.1.0 exposes a UI server endpoint with no authorization check — any network-reachable origin can read arbitrary files from the developer's filesystem and trigger code execution. CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N). The declared range ^2.1.9 resolves entirely within the vulnerable range (<4.1.0). The `test` npm script invokes vitest directly, so every CI run and local test session is affected; the UI server (vitest --ui) compounds the risk to RCE.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump to vitest >=4.1.8 (latest stable): `npm install --save-dev vitest@^4.1.8`. Note: this is a semver-major jump — review vitest 4.x migration notes for any API breakage. Fix also resolves the transitive esbuild and vite-node advisories that chain through vitest.

findings.title: download_url host-prefix check does not constrain repo path — any GitHub-hosted binary passes

Combined with the intentional absence of signature/hash verification, the NSIS binary that gets launched via openPath() is entirely unverified. The threat requires controlling the API response or
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the path prefix check to require the known releases repo: assert the URL contains '/Blazzer10200/rift-releases/' after the host. Additionally, publish a SHA-256 checksum in the release body or as a sidecar asset and verify it post-download before calling openPath. This is defense-in-depth given TLS already protects the transport, but closes the gap opened by the no-signing-key design.

findings.title: Model name validated by character allowlist only — arbitrary model IDs accepted
findings.description: is_valid_model_name accepts any non-empty string matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ that does not start with a dash. This allows an arbitrary model identifier (e.g. claude-internal-endpoint, a future alias, or a typo-squatted name) to flow into --model. While the character set prevents flag injection (no leading dash, no spaces, no shell metacharacters), a compromised renderer or malicious IPC call can direct spend to unintended API endpoints. The summarize path applies a strict three-value allowlist (haiku|sonnet|opus) but assistant_send does not.

findings.title: $effect reads fracs (drag state) as a dependency while also assigning fracs
findings.description: The $effect at line 94 is meant to re-sync `fracs` when the pane count changes, but it reads `fracs.length` on line 96 to guard the reassignment. This makes `fracs` a tracked reactive dependency of the effect. Every time the user drags a pane divider (line 163: `fracs = next`) the effect re-fires: it reads `fracs.length`, the guard is false (pane count unchanged), so no infinite write — but the effect body executes on every drag-position update, which fires continuously at pointer-move frequency. In a three-pane split with rapid dragging this means tens of spurious effect runs per second, each
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `fracs` from the effect's reactive scope by reading it through `$state.snapshot` or by untracking it with `untrack(() => fracs.length)`. Alternatively restructure: `const prevN = $state(0); $effect(() => { const n = assistant.panes.length || 1; if (n !== prevN) { prevN = n; fracs = loadFracs(n); } });` — this way only `assistant.panes.length` and `prevN` are subscribed, and `fracs` is never read inside the effect.

findings.title: $effect clamps activeIdx by reading it as a tracked dependency then writing it
findings.description: The $effect at line 184 subscribes to both `flat.length` and `activeIdx` (reading it in the comparison), then conditionally writes `activeIdx`. Any keyboard navigation that changes `activeIdx` (e.g. ArrowDown at line 197: `activeIdx = (activeIdx + 1) % flat.length`) immediately re-triggers this effect. The write path only fires when `activeIdx >= flat.length`, so there is no infinite loop when the list is stable, but the effect body re-executes on every cursor movement even though the list length has not changed. With a long list and fast key repeat this creates unnecessary reactive churn and
findings.suggested_fix: Read `activeIdx` with `untrack` to break the self-subscription: `$effect(() => { const len = flat.length; untrack(() => { if (activeIdx >= len) activeIdx = Math.max(0, len - 1); }); });`. This makes the effect react only to `flat.length` changes (i.e. filter results narrowing), not to every cursor movement.
